city.name: Shibuya
city.description: Shibuya, Harajuku and Yoyogi Park, out to Sangenjaya's backstreets: the scramble and Hachiko, the city from SHIBUYA SKY, Center Gai's arcades and the streets a famous game drew.

tour.title: Sangenjaya to Harajuku
tour.text: Youth culture's Tokyo: fashion on Takeshita Street, the forest of Meiji Jingu, the busiest crossing on Earth, and out west the izakaya alleys of Sangenjaya where the city goes home to drink.

tour.title: The scramble
tour.text: When the lights change, every crossing turns green at once, the diagonals too, and up to three thousand people cross together. Watch it from above, then join in. Hachiko sits to the south, waiting for his master, as he did for ten years.

tour.title: SHIBUYA SKY, 229 m
tour.text: An open-air deck on Scramble Square's roof, glass at the edge and nothing above you but sky. Come at sunset: Mount Fuji on the horizon, then Tokyo lighting up beneath your feet.

tour.title: Sangenjaya's triangle
tour.text: Between Setagaya-dori and Route 246: a bathhouse, a snack bar, a meat shop open all night. A game drew its hero's home town here and called it Yongen-Jaya; fans still come looking for the café.

protection.title: No sun-access rule for public places
protection.summary: Tokyo protects no park's sunlight. The windows are a lunch-hour thought experiment for this project, as in the Marunouchi model.
protection.source_note: Windows are our own choice (noon to 13:00, all year), not law. The Building Standards Act's shadow rule (日影規制, art. 56-2) limits hours of shadow on neighbouring land in residential-type zones; it does not cover public places and does not apply in commercial districts such as Shibuya.
protection.reading_note: Tokyo keeps standard time all year. Miyashita Park is a roof garden on a mall (2020): its sun here is read at the ground, so treat it with care.
protection.tip: Tip: try a tower on the block south of Yoyogi Park, west of Harajuku Station.

light_show.name: CROSSING LIGHT
light_show.note: SHIBUYA SKY's 18 searchlights: shows from 19:00 on the hour and the half hour, to 22:00 (enjoytokyo, nippon.com). Each show's length and the beams' movement here are illustrative.

shore.encoding: r: 128 + 2 x signed distance to the shoreline (m, water positive); g: sand; b: rock

susuki.note: Susuki (trees.json susuki, #326): on the open grassland and meadows OpenStreetMap maps (natural=grassland, landuse=meadow: the unmown grass of the parks and the hills, where susuki is the grass that stands) (Overture base land, OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL; pipeline/grasses.py). Its heads stand from mid August to spring (web/trees.js).

trees.note: Species are not mapped; the mix is a guess from the cities' street-tree surveys and the parks' own guides: ginkgo and zelkova (keyaki) are Japan's commonest street trees, with plane trees and camphor; the woods are the laurel forest's evergreen broadleaves and camphors, with zelkovas, black pines, maples and a few cedars (sugi, standing for hinoki too). Areas give the parks and precincts known for their own trees a mix of their own; their outlines are OpenStreetMap's (pipeline/tree_areas.py). Somei-yoshino cherries (sakura) line Tokyo's streets after the ginkgo and the zelkova, and stand in the parks' lawns and along the rivers and moats; areas give the places known for them a mix of their own.

areas.name: Hachiko Square's planters
areas.note: The round planter north of Hachiko holds a Somei-yoshino (photographs 2020-25).

areas.name: Hachiko Square's planters, south
areas.note: And so does the one south of him.

areas.name: Meguro River
areas.note: About 800 cherries on both banks from Ikejiri-Ohashi down through Nakameguro, their branches over the water (Meguro City). In the bloom pink chochin hang along both railings and the cherries are lit after dark (#241): the area is the river's line buffered 14 m, so the railings, about 5.5 m either side of it, are 8.5 m inside the outline.

areas.name: Meiji Jingu
areas.note: The planted shrine forest, now mostly camphor and the evergreen oaks and shii of the laurel forest.

signs.note: shop signs on street fronts in the districts; indicative, not the real shops' signs
